newsitem.title: UK: Sinking lira volatility shows broad EMU expected.
newsitem.headline: Sinking lira volatility shows broad EMU expected.

text.p: The level of lira volatility expected by the options market is fast falling to French franc levels and is one of the clearest signals that investors are now betting European economic and monetary union will have a broad-based starting membership, analysts said.

The one-month implied volatility for the mark/lira cross rate, which was up to 35 percent just over two years ago, fell to a record low of just 3.15/65 percent on Monday and dragged one-year implied volatility down to 4.0/4.5 percent too.

"The collapse of lira option volatility is a direct reflection of the market belief that Italy, and the other "Club Med" countries, will now start EMU in 1999," said Stewart Newnham, economist at First Chicago in London.

Analysts said mark/lira volatility is converging on French franc levels. Given the market assumption that France is an automatic candidate for the first wave of EMU, mark/franc vols are as low as 1.5 percent for both one-month and one-year.
The vol price bias in favour of lira puts has almost halved this year to stand at 0.5/1.1 percentage points on Monday.
Mark/peseta implied vol too has tumbled to historically low levels, 2.20/2.80 percent on a one-month horizon and just 3.60/3.80 percent over one year.

The spread between Italian and Spanish vols and their Swedish equivalents, which are currently 6.20/6.70 percent for one-month, illustrates the degree of EMU optimism factored into the price, traders said.
Contrary to the intense political will behind EMU in Madrid and Rome, the Swedish government decided to rule itself out of the first EMU wave earlier this month.

"We are seeing a lot of buying of lira assets and switching out of other European markets on the argument that it's now increasingly certain EMU will start with a wide membership," said Michael Burke, economist at Citibank in London.
The spread between 10-year Italian and German government bond yields fell to a record low at 118 basis points on Monday.
At 1430 GMT, mark/lira was trading at 978.20/50 just off a four-month low at 976.60 set earlier in the session.
Analysts said the latest convergence has been enhanced by the election of a Socialist government in France earlier this month and by the Amsterdam European Union summit last week.
The French government's call for a more inclusive start to EMU in 1999 received little opposition at the summit and there are signs Germany is being persuaded to its way of thinking.
German CDU parliament leader Wolfgang Schaeuble reinforced this shift over the weekend.

The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung also said Schaeuble warned Germany against being "arrogant" towards other EU nations en route to the single currency and said differences of decimal points in meeting the EMU budgetary criteria were not decisive.
"People were very long of mark/lira vol and lira puts for some time and we're now finally seeing an unwinding of those positions," said one options trader at a UK bank in London.
"This is all stemming from the Amsterdam summit, which convinced many people that EMU will have a broad-based start."
